explanation: Faithfully states Erdős's claimed ε = 1/2 case from erdosproblems.com/1201. For every η > 0 there is k such that the set of n with P(n(n+1)⋯(n+k)) > n^{1/2} has lower density at least 1 - η, with the liminf taken in EReal. P(m) is the sSup of the prime divisors, which is the true maximum for n ≥ 1. The n = 0 junk value does not affect density.
